title: Plans to strengthen peer support for mental health in communities and workplaces
asked: Ms Elysa Chen asked whether there are plans to strengthen and resource peer support structures for mental health in community settings and workplaces, including training, supervision and safeguards for peer supporters so that early help is more accessible while ensuring peer supporters are not over-burdened or placed in situations beyond their competencies.
response: Dr Koh Poh Koon said HPB runs peer support training for institutes of higher learning, workplaces and community groups, teaching participants to recognise distress, listen actively and guide peers to seek help early. From this year, HPB training will be hybrid and include additional modules, while NCSS trains peer support specialists with lived experience, MOM and the WSH Council run a Well-being Champions Network, and AIC offers online mental health awareness modules. He said peer support is one part of the support scaffold and is not meant to carry the burden of professional mental health care; if a peer supporter reaches the limits of their competency, resources such as mindline.sg can be referral points. In supplementary replies, he said peer support is an informal scaffold rather than part of the formalised care structure, and that for harder-to-reach groups the focus is on education and community care teams.

key_points.point: HPB offers peer support training for institutes of higher learning, workplaces and community groups.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: the Health Promotion Board (HPB) offers peer support training for institutes of higher learning (IHLs), workplaces and community groups.

key_points.point: Participants are trained to recognise peers in distress, provide active listening and guide them to seek help early.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: Participants are trained to recognise peers in distress, provide active listening and guide them to seek help early.

key_points.point: From this year, HPB peer supporter training will be available in a hybrid format and offer additional modules.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: From this year onwards, HPB's peer supporter training will be available in a hybrid format and offer additional modules to enhance training.

key_points.point: NCSS runs a peer support specialist programme for persons with lived experience to support others in recovery.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: the National Council of Social Service's (NCSS') peer support specialist programme trains persons with lived experiences to support others on their recovery journeys.

key_points.point: MOM and the WSH Council established the Well-being Champions Network to provide workplace-appointed Champions with resources and training.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: The Ministry of Manpower (MOM) and the Workplace Safety and Health (WSH) Council have established the Well-being Champions Network to provide workplace-appointed Champions with the necessary resources and training to better support their organisations in promoting workplace mental health well-being.

key_points.point: AIC offers online mental health awareness modules to equip frontliners to help persons with mental health needs navigate services.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: The Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) also offers online mental health awareness modules to better equip frontliners to help persons with mental health needs navigate the service landscape.

key_points.point: Peer support is not meant to carry the burden of mental health care that professionals should do.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: They are not meant to carry the burden of mental health care that the professionals should be doing.

key_points.point: If a peer supporter reaches the limits of their competency, resources such as mindline.sg can be referral points.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: if a peer supporter feels that there is something beyond which his or her competency can handle, then I think these resources we put forth, like mindline.sg, can be useful referral points

key_points.point: Peer support is an informal scaffold around formal levels of support, not part of the formalised care structure.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: peer support is meant to be an informal scaffold around formal levels of support and I think we should not put a burden on them to be part of the formalised care structure.

key_points.point: For harder-to-reach groups, the focus is on increasing education and using community care teams to reach out and encourage care-seeking.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: the focus for us would be to increase education and also to put forth our community care teams

left_open: Targeted outreach or tailored peer support initiatives for older adults, caregivers and persons in lower wage or precarious employment
supplementary: Integrating peer support into the tiered care model and reaching groups less likely to use formal services.
